마트.x: I do grocery shopping at the supermarket on weekends.
마트.e: From English 'mart'. Means a big supermarket, not a small corner shop.

커피.x: Shall we have a cup of coffee?
커피.e: From English 'coffee'. Sounds like 'keopi' — Korean has no f sound.

빨래.x: I have to do the laundry today.

별로.forms: 별로 + negative: 별로 안 좋아해요 · alone: 별로예요 (not great)
별로.ex: 저는 매운 음식을 별로 안 좋아해요.
별로.x: I don't really like spicy food.
별로.e: 별 special + 로 — 'not specially'. Not 별 (star).
별로.t: Almost always used with a negative. 별로예요 on its own means 'It's not that good.'

도로.x: The roads are very slippery because of the snow.
도로.t: 도로 is a road for vehicles and sounds more formal; 길 is the everyday word for road or way.

돌다.forms: 돌아요 · 돌았어요 · 돌 거예요 · 도세요 (ㄹ drops)
돌다.m: to turn; to go around, to spin
돌다.x: Turn left in front of the bank over there.
돌다.t: The ㄹ drops before -세요: say 도세요, not 돌으세요.
rel: to go back, to go around

위험하다.ex: 밤에 혼자 산에 가는 것은 위험해요.
위험하다.x: Going to the mountains alone at night is dangerous.

드라이브.x: The weather was nice, so we went for a drive to the beach.
드라이브.e: From English 'drive', but only for a leisure drive; everyday driving is 운전.
드라이브.t: Common patterns: 드라이브(를) 가다 'go for a drive' and 드라이브하다.

소설.ex: 요즘 재미있는 한국 소설을 읽고 있어요.
소설.x: These days I'm reading an interesting Korean novel.
소설.e: Literally 'small talk' — once considered minor stories, not serious writing.

무늬.x: The pattern on this shirt is really pretty.
무늬.e: Combines with nouns: 꽃무늬 'floral print', 줄무늬 'stripes'.
무늬.t: Pronounced [무니]; ㅢ after a consonant sounds like ㅣ.

맞히다.m: to get (an answer) right, to guess correctly; to hit (a target)
맞히다.ex: 이 문제의 정답을 맞힌 사람이 없어요.
맞히다.x: Nobody got the right answer to this question.
맞히다.e: Causative of 맞다 'to be correct' — literally 'make it correct'.
맞히다.t: Don't mix up with 맞추다 'to match or fit'; for answers, standard Korean uses 맞히다.

하루.e: Native day count: 하루 (1), 이틀 (2), 사흘 (3), 나흘 (4).
하루.t: 하루 종일 means 'all day long' — a very common phrase.

번째.forms: 첫 번째 · 두 번째 · 세 번째
번째.x: This is my second trip to Korea.
번째.t: Use native numbers: 첫 번째 (not 한 번째), 두 번째, 세 번째.

편찮으시다.m: to be unwell, to be sick (honorific)
편찮으시다.x: My grandmother has been quite unwell lately.
편찮으시다.e: 편찮다 is short for 편하지 않다 'not comfortable', plus the honorific -(으)시-.
편찮으시다.t: Pronounced [편차느시다]: ㅎ is silent before a vowel. The plain word is 아프다; use 편찮으시다 for parents, grandparents and other elders, never for yourself.

오염.x: The river pollution got worse because of the factory.

분류하다.m: to classify, to sort, to categorize
분류하다.x: Sort your trash by type before throwing it out.
분류하다.t: Pronounced [불류하다] — ㄴ becomes ㄹ before ㄹ.

점검.ex: 엘리베이터 점검 때문에 계단을 이용해 주세요.
점검.x: Due to elevator inspection, please use the stairs.
점검.e: Literally 'tick off and examine' — check item by item.

문화 충격.ex: 한국에 처음 왔을 때 문화 충격을 받았어요.
문화 충격.x: When I first came to Korea, I experienced culture shock.
문화 충격.e: A direct translation of English 'culture shock': 문화 'culture' + 충격 'shock'.
문화 충격.t: The usual verb is 받다: 문화 충격을 받다, 'to experience culture shock'.

다툼.x: A small quarrel turned into a big fight.
다툼.e: Noun form of 다투다 'to argue' plus -ㅁ.

예외.x: There isn't a single exception to this rule.
예외.e: Literally 'outside the examples' — the case that doesn't fit.

엠티.ex: 다음 주에 과 친구들이랑 엠티 가요.
엠티.x: Next week I'm going on an MT with friends from my department.
엠티.e: Konglish: from the initials of English 'membership training', also written MT.
엠티.t: Usually an overnight trip to a rented country guesthouse with games, cooking and drinking, especially common for freshmen in the spring semester.

밀리리터.x: This cup holds 300 milliliters of water.
밀리리터.t: In everyday speech people often shorten it to 미리: 오백 미리 생수 'a 500 ml bottle of water'.

지점.ex: 이 은행 지점은 오후 4시에 문을 닫아요.
지점.x: This bank branch closes at 4 p.m.

규범.ex: 사회 규범을 지키는 것은 모두에게 중요해요.
규범.x: Following social norms is important for everyone.

진로.x: High school students worry a lot about their future path.
진로.t: Pronounced [질로] — ㄴ becomes ㄹ next to ㄹ.

식목일.x: On Arbor Day, I planted trees with my family.
식목일.e: Literally 'tree-planting day'; no longer a public holiday since 2006.
식목일.t: Pronounced [싱모길]: nasalization turns ㄱ into ㅇ before ㅁ.

탄소 중립.x: The government announced it will achieve carbon neutrality by 2050.
탄소 중립.e: 탄소 'carbon' plus 중립 'neutrality', literally 'standing in the middle'.
탄소 중립.t: 중립 is pronounced [중닙]: ㄹ becomes ㄴ after the ㅇ batchim.

폐지.x: The government decided to abolish that system.
폐지.t: Homonym: 폐지 (a different word) also means 'waste paper', as in 폐지 줍기.

유산.ex: 할아버지가 남기신 유산으로 작은 집을 샀어요.
유산.x: We bought a small house with the inheritance my grandfather left.
유산.e: Literally 'property left behind'. Homonym warning: another 유산 means miscarriage.

눈이 높다.forms: 눈이 높아요 · 눈이 높았어요 · 눈이 높은 사람
눈이 높다.m: to have high standards, to be picky
눈이 높다.ex: 언니는 눈이 높아서 아직 남자 친구가 없어요.
눈이 높다.x: My older sister has high standards, so she still doesn't have a boyfriend.

가슴이 뜨끔하다.forms: 가슴이 뜨끔해요 · 가슴이 뜨끔했어요 · 가슴이 뜨끔한 (+noun)
가슴이 뜨끔하다.m: to feel a pang of guilt, to be stung (by a remark)
가슴이 뜨끔하다.ex: 거짓말을 한 게 생각나서 가슴이 뜨끔했어요.
가슴이 뜨끔하다.x: I remembered the lie I'd told and felt a pang of guilt.
가슴이 뜨끔하다.e: 뜨끔하다 describes a sudden prick or sting, like a needle; here it's a sting of conscience.
nb: 발 없는 말이 천 리 간다

본질.x: We need to grasp the essence of the problem accurately.
본질.e: Literally 'original substance': what something really is underneath.

전제.ex: 두 사람은 결혼을 전제로 사귀고 있어요.
전제.x: The two of them are dating with marriage in mind.
전제.e: Literally 'put forward beforehand': what you lay down first.
전제.t: Common pattern: N을/를 전제로 'on the premise of N, with N in mind'.

쿠폰.ex: 생일 쿠폰을 받아서 커피를 무료로 마셨어요.
쿠폰.x: I got a birthday coupon, so I had coffee for free.

조선.x: Gyeongbokgung is a palace built in the Joseon era.
조선.e: Literally 'morning freshness', the source of the phrase 'Land of the Morning Calm'.
조선.t: 조선 시대 = the Joseon era, the setting of most historical dramas. It was renamed the Korean Empire (대한제국) in 1897.

칼퇴.x: I have plans today, so I'm leaving work right on time.
칼퇴.e: Short for 칼퇴근: 칼 'knife' + 퇴근 'leaving work' — leaving as sharply and precisely as a knife cuts.
칼퇴.t: Casual. Seen as a mark of good 워라밸, the opposite of 야근. Verb: 칼퇴하다.

사임.x: The minister took responsibility for the accident and resigned.
사임.t: 사임 is formal and used for officials; for quitting an ordinary job, say 그만두다.

에너지원.x: Solar power is getting attention as a clean energy source.

구도.m: composition (of a picture); structure, framework (of a situation)
구도.x: This photo has a stable composition.
구도.t: In news, 구도 means the shape of a situation: 양강 구도 is a two-way race.

야기하다.m: to cause, to give rise to, to provoke
야기하다.x: His remarks caused a big controversy.
야기하다.t: Homonym warning: 이야기 (story) is unrelated; 야기하다 is a formal written verb.

권고하다.x: The doctor advised him to quit drinking.
권고하다.t: More official than 권하다; common in news: 정부는 외출 자제를 권고했다.

고무하다.m: to inspire, to hearten, to boost (morale)
고무하다.x: His speech inspired many young people.
고무하다.e: Literally 'drum and dance' — rousing people like festival music.
고무하다.t: Often 고무되다 'to be heartened'; don't confuse it with 고무 'rubber.'

다그치다.m: to press, to push (someone to hurry or answer); to grill
다그치다.ex: 엄마가 숙제를 빨리 하라고 아이를 다그쳤어요.
다그치다.x: The mom pushed her child to hurry up and do the homework.
다그치다.t: Often with quotes: 빨리 하라고 다그치다 'push to hurry', 왜 그랬냐고 다그치다 'demand to know why'.

유해하다.x: Cigarette smoke is harmful to your health.
유해하다.t: Formal and written; the everyday word is 해롭다.

더군다나.forms: A. 더군다나 B. — stronger than 게다가, often with 까지
더군다나.m: what's more, on top of that, besides
더군다나.ex: 그는 돈이 없었고, 더군다나 일자리까지 잃었어요.
더군다나.x: He had no money, and on top of that, he lost his job.

가지런히.m: neatly, evenly, in a tidy row
가지런히.x: Please line your shoes up neatly at the entrance.

주경야독.m: working by day and studying by night
주경야독.x: After years of working by day and studying by night, he graduated from college.
주경야독.e: Literally 'plow by day, read by night.'

눈 밖에 나다.forms: 눈 밖에 나요 · 눈 밖에 났어요 · ~의 눈 밖에 나다
눈 밖에 나다.m: to fall out of favor with someone; to get on someone's bad side
눈 밖에 나다.ex: 지각을 자주 해서 사장님 눈 밖에 났어요.
눈 밖에 나다.x: I was late so often that I got on the boss's bad side.
눈 밖에 나다.e: Literally 'to go outside someone's eyes' — out of their good graces.
눈 밖에 나다.t: Opposite: 눈에 들다 'to catch someone's eye, win favor.'

휴재.ex: 작가님 건강 문제로 이번 주는 휴재래요.
휴재.x: They say there's no episode this week because of the artist's health.
휴재.e: Literally 'rest from publishing'; the opposite of 연재.
휴재.t: 휴재하다 = to go on hiatus; platforms post a 휴재 공지 'hiatus notice'.

심란하다.m: to be unsettled, troubled, restless in mind
심란하다.ex: 이사 문제로 요즘 마음이 좀 심란해요.
심란하다.x: I've been feeling pretty unsettled lately over the move.
심란하다.t: Pronounced [심난하다] — ㄹ after ㅁ becomes ㄴ.

수율.ex: 새 공정 덕분에 반도체 수율이 크게 높아졌습니다.
수율.x: Thanks to the new process, the chip yield rose significantly.
수율.e: Literally 'gathered rate' — the share of usable output.
수율.t: A key word in chip-industry news; 수율이 높다 means more good chips per wafer.

사회기반시설.ex: 정부는 도로와 철도 같은 사회기반시설에 투자하고 있습니다.
사회기반시설.x: The government is investing in infrastructure such as roads and railways.
사회기반시설.t: In speech and news, the loanword 인프라 is used much more often.

화소.ex: 이 카메라는 화소가 높아서 사진이 선명해요.
화소.x: This camera has a high pixel count, so photos are sharp.
화소.e: Literally 'picture element' — exactly what 'pixel' stands for.
화소.t: Camera specs use 만 화소: 1200만 화소 means 12 megapixels.

전개.ex: 이 드라마는 이야기 전개가 빨라서 지루하지 않아요.
전개.x: This drama's story moves quickly, so it isn't boring.
전개.e: Literally 'unfold and open' — the stage where the story moves forward.
전개.t: The classic plot stages are 발단, 전개, 위기, 절정, 결말.

주해.ex: 이 고전은 주해가 자세해서 읽기 쉬워요.
주해.x: This classic is easy to read because its annotations are detailed.
주해.e: Literally 'note and explain' — notes that explain a difficult text.

개화.ex: 개화를 주장한 사람들은 서양의 기술을 배우자고 했어요.
개화.x: Those who called for enlightenment urged learning Western technology.
개화.t: Homonym: 개화 also means flowers blooming, written with different characters.

철기.m: iron tools, ironware; the Iron Age
철기.ex: 철기가 보급되면서 농업 생산량이 크게 늘었습니다.
철기.x: As iron tools spread, agricultural output increased greatly.

구가하다.m: to enjoy (to the fullest), to bask in (prosperity, success)
구가하다.ex: 그 회사는 최근 최고의 호황을 구가하고 있습니다.
구가하다.x: The company is currently enjoying its best boom ever.
구가하다.e: Literally 'sing praises' — singing about your good times.
구가하다.t: Typical objects: 자유, 전성기, 호황, 인기 — something good you are enjoying.

안주하다.m: to settle down; to be complacent, to rest on one's laurels
안주하다.x: Don't settle for where you are now; keep challenging yourself.
안주하다.t: Homonym: 안주 (按酒) means snacks eaten with alcohol.

회고하다.m: to look back on, to recall, to reminisce
회고하다.ex: 그는 어린 시절을 회고하며 책을 썼어요.
회고하다.x: He wrote a book looking back on his childhood.

도래하다.m: to arrive, to come (an era, a time)
도래하다.ex: 이제 우리 사회에도 인공지능 시대가 도래했습니다.
도래하다.x: The age of artificial intelligence has now arrived in our society too.

필시.ex: 연락이 없는 걸 보니 필시 무슨 일이 생긴 거예요.
필시.x: Since there's no word from him, something must have happened.
필시.t: Signals a strong guess, usually with -ㄹ 것이다 or -ㄴ 게 틀림없다.

넘나들다.forms: 넘나들어요 · 넘나들었어요 · 넘나들 거예요 · 넘나드세요 (ㄹ drops)
넘나들다.m: to go back and forth (across), to cross freely between
넘나들다.ex: 그 배우는 영화와 연극을 자유롭게 넘나들어요.
넘나들다.x: That actor moves freely between film and theater.
넘나들다.e: 넘다 'cross over' + 나다 'go out' + 들다 'come in' — crossing back and forth.
넘나들다.t: Common with 경계 'boundary': 장르의 경계를 넘나들다 'to cross genre boundaries'.

괴리.ex: 정치인과 국민의 생각 사이에 괴리가 커요.
괴리.x: There's a big disconnect between what politicians and citizens think.

지리멸렬.x: His explanation was so incoherent that it was hard to understand.
지리멸렬.t: Pronounced [지리멸렬] with a double ㄹ sound; used with 하다 or 되다.
